Department of Computer Science and Engineering
Md. Bokhtiar Rahman Juboraz (20301138) | Md. Mahir Ahnaf Ahmed (20301083)
Supervisor: Mr. Annajiat Alim Rasel, Senior Lecturer, Dept. of CSE, BRAC University

Modern institutional banking is organized in restrictive layers that limit equal access to financing. Crypto World Bank (CWB) specifies a four-tier, hierarchically-governed DeFi platform — World Bank reserve → National → Local Banks → Clients — mirroring real-world development finance while enforcing reserves, credit allocation, and risk analytics on-chain. Six on-chain banking functions (deposits, credit allocation, settlement, risk intermediation, liquidity management, ancillary services) sit behind a five-layer defense-in-depth security model. ) and an optional MCP-based conversational agent enhance security and usability, showing a transparent, open-source alternative to flat DeFi lending is achievable.

Layered institutions (World → National → Local → Client) suffer settlement friction, opaque reserves, and idle correspondent-banking capital; flat DeFi (Aave, Compound, MakerDAO) ignores this hierarchy entirely.
Encode institutional hierarchy on a programmable ledger — enforced reserves, role-based governance, auditable capital flow — supporting (not replacing) human credit judgment.
Six inefficiencies: low transparency, slow/costly settlement (~$45, 2–5 days), inconsistent risk evaluation, high trust/audit costs, no programmable savings, no on-chain group credit.
Specify a 4-tier EVM lending architecture with an extended banking suite, off-chain ML risk analytics, and an optional conversational agent; deploy and evaluate on testnets.
